lesson.title: Learn: two verb forms that act like nouns

items.title: Gerund = verb-ing as a noun
lines: It can be a subject or an object.
chips: Playing tennis is fun. (subject)
We enjoy playing tennis. (object of a verb)
He's excited about playing tennis. (object of a preposition)

items.title: Not every -ing is a gerund
lines: Progressive verbs and adjectives also end in -ing.
chips: Walking is good exercise. ✅ gerund
Bob and Ann are playing tennis. ❌ verb
That was a surprising win. ❌ adjective

items.text: “Running uphill is hard work.” Running is…
items.why: It is the subject of is → a gerund.

items.title: Infinitive = to + simple verb
lines: Usually it is the object.
chips: He likes to play tennis. (object)
To play tennis well takes a lot of practice. (subject)

items.title: to is not always an infinitive
lines: to + noun = a preposition.
chips: Marta needs to leave early. ✅ infinitive
Is Elias committed to his job? ❌ preposition

items.text: “Franco is engaged to Liz.” Here, to is…

lines: Gerund = verb-ing used as a noun: Playing tennis is fun.
Infinitive = to + simple verb: He likes to play tennis.

examples.text: Playing tennis is fun.
We enjoy playing tennis.
He likes to play tennis.

items.why: The subject of is → a gerund.

items.word: Would you consider SCHEDULING a practice in the evening?

items.why: The subject of is → a gerund.

talk.title: Plans and promises
talk.task: Claude asks: What do you need to do today? What do you plan to do with English?
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English speaking partner. Ask me one question at a time: What do you need to do today? What would you like to do this weekend? What do you plan to do with English? What should people refuse to do? What shouldn't people pretend to do? What should students expect to do? I answer in full sentences with verb + to + verb. talk.title: The birdhouse
talk.task: Thomas tried to build a birdhouse for his wife. It went badly! Tell Claude the story.
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English speaking partner. Situation: Thomas wanted to build a birdhouse for his wife, Eleni. Ask me to make sentences about it, one verb at a time: intend, forget, remember, keep on, regret, stop, advise, encourage, offer, suggest, consider, finish. Example: He intended to finish it in an hour. She advised him to stop. Check whether each verb takes to + verb, -ing, or person + to + verb.

talk.title: It's easy for me to…
talk.task: Tell Claude what is easy, hard, important, or a good idea for you.
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English speaking partner. Ask me to finish one sentence at a time about myself: It is easy for me to ... / It isn't easy for me to ... / It is important for students to ... / It's a good idea for visitors to my country to ... / It is difficult for me to .... After each, ask me to say the same idea with a gerund subject (Speaking in class is difficult for me.). Check: It is + adjective + for + person + to + verb, and a singular verb after a gerund subject.

talk.title: Thank-you note
talk.task: Write a short thank-you note after a job interview. Claude checks it.
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English writing partner. Situation: Henry Sanson interviewed with Ms. Azizi for the position of hotel assistant manager. He has a recent degree in hotel management and one year's experience as a front desk clerk. Ask me to write Henry's thank-you note in 5-6 sentences using: thank you for + -ing, enjoy + -ing, be interested in + -ing, have the opportunity + to, look forward to + -ing. Check each gerund and infinitive and the polite closing.
